title: FDA Approvals Based on Basket, Umbrella and Platform Trials: What Reviewers Said About Master Protocols
summary: FDA approvals supported by basket, umbrella and platform trials, and what agency reviewers said about the strengths and weaknesses of master protocol designs.
body_markdown:
## FDA approvals based on basket, umbrella and platform trials: what reviewers said about master protocol designs


Master protocols have supported a distinct set of FDA approvals. Most of the examples reviewed here are in oncology, where single-arm basket cohorts have supported tissue-agnostic and tumor-specific accelerated approvals. Outside oncology there are several high-profile examples: the PALM Ebola master protocol, the SURMOUNT-OSA "basket-type" master protocol for tirzepatide, and the RECOVERY platform study cited in tocilizumab labeling. Umbrella designs appear in the records reviewed only in a supportive role (Litfulo). Across these files, FDA reviewers have consistently credited the designs with efficiency, biological coherence and feasibility in rare populations. They have just as consistently pointed to the same weaknesses: single-arm data that cannot interpret time-to-event endpoints, sparse tumor-type representation, unreliable subgroup estimates, pooling that can undercut independent substantiation, and shared-control choices that complicate interpretation.


### How FDA defines the designs


FDA's March 2022 final oncology guidance, *Master Protocols: Efficient Clinical Trial Design Strategies to Expedite Development of Oncology Drugs and Biologics* , and the June 2026 cross-therapeutic draft, *Master Protocols for Drug and Biological Product Development* , set out the working vocabulary[599](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=599)[582](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=582)[602](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=602) :


- **Basket trial:** one drug evaluated across multiple diseases, conditions or disease subtypes[603](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=603) . In oncology, the populations can differ by cancer, stage, histology, prior therapy, biomarker or demographics[604](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=604) .
- **Umbrella trial:** multiple drugs evaluated concurrently in a single disease or condition[605](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=605)[606](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=606) .
- **Platform trial:** an ongoing trial of multiple drugs for one or more diseases, with drugs entering or leaving the platform[607](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=607) . A platform can include both basket and umbrella components, so the categories overlap[608](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=608) .


The guidance also addresses issues that reviewers raised in individual applications. A common control arm should reflect current standard of care, and enrollment should be suspended if that standard changes[609](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=609) . Primary comparisons should generally use only concurrently eligible controls[587](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=587) . Multiple groups invite overinterpretation, including false apparent subgroup differences[611](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=611) . Basket substudies are usually single-arm, ORR-based and need their own sample-size justification and stopping rules[613](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=613) .

### Tissue-agnostic approvals built on pooled basket evidence


#### Pembrolizumab for MSI-H/dMMR cancers


The MSI-H/dMMR review describes the first approval independent of cancer type and based solely on a tumor biomarker[154](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=154) . Reviewers justified pooling five trials, two doses and 16 tumor types on the basis of consistent demographic and baseline characteristics and consistent response rate and durability across trials[281](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=281)[305](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=305) . The team leader considered the evidence substantial because durable objective responses, confirmed by independent radiology review, were seen across multiple trials, multiple MSI-H/dMMR cancers and sites in and outside the United States[668](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=668) .


Reviewers were direct about the limitations:


- The protocols contained no sample-size justification, and all studies were ongoing. Decisions would rest on the ORR point estimate and 95% CI, not formal hypothesis testing[671](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=671) .
- Between-trial differences could reflect chance, population, site or design rather than dose, given the nonrandomized design and limited numbers[672](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=672) .
- Tumor-specific results "may not be reliable" because of sample size. Their value was in showing breadth across tumor types, not in establishing efficacy in each cancer[673](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=673) .
- The reviewer warned that this approval should not imply that every biomarker-targeted drug merits a site-agnostic indication, because tumor-specific resistance mechanisms and treatment context could alter benefit[674](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=674) .


#### Larotrectinib and entrectinib for NTRK fusion-positive tumors


The NTRK reviews follow the same template. For larotrectinib, FDA identified limited efficacy numbers (N=55) and a small safety population (N=176), with patients enrolled sequentially across multiple single-arm trials, as review challenges[148](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=148) . Strong scientific rationale, nonclinical evidence and consistent durable shrinkage across tumors and fusion partners justified pooling[149](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=149) . FDA accepted that effects in underrepresented tumors, including lung and colon cancers, were less well characterized, and required additional evidence because of the many histologies and the small efficacy database[150](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=150)[151](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=151) . It also cautioned that limited exploratory subgroup sizes prevented interpretation of numerical ORR differences across tumor types and fusion subgroups[286](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=286)[311](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=311) . Reviewers further noted that response rate and duration might not fully capture benefit, citing complete radiographic disappearance and limb-sparing surgery in some patients[180](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=180) .


The entrectinib review (NDA 212726) repeats these points. Small efficacy (N=54) and safety (N=355) populations were limitations[184](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=184) . Pooling was warranted by biological rationale, nonclinical activity across cell lines and fusion partners, and consistent durable shrinkage[186](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=186) . Effects in pediatric and CNS cancers were less well characterized[187](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=187) , and postapproval data were needed to improve confidence across tumor types[188](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=188) . Reviewers also explained why randomization was not the answer: extreme rarity, differing natural histories, limited equipoise and expected crossover made randomized trials challenging, and combining all tumor types in one randomized trial might not be scientifically appropriate[189](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=189) .


In the 2023 pediatric expansion (NDA 218550), reviewers said the two single-arm trials were pooled "due to the rarity of the population"[474](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=474) . They reported prespecified analyses, no major statistical issues and BICR to minimize measurement bias[475](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=475)[476](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=476) . They noted that the small population made it hard to tell whether response differed between CNS and non-CNS tumors[479](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=479) , and attached a postmarketing requirement to verify benefit[480](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=480) .


#### Selpercatinib, dostarlimab and trastuzumab deruxtecan


For selpercatinib's RET fusion tissue-agnostic indication, FDA acknowledged variable response rates in tumor-specific groups of 1 to 11 patients. It still considered the indication appropriate given clinically meaningful responses across tumor types and the existing NSCLC and thyroid cancer evidence[134](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=134) . Reviewers flagged uncertainty about response magnitude in extremely rare or unrepresented tumors and the lower colorectal response rate, and required additional cross-tumor evidence postmarketing[135](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=135) . A randomized trial was considered infeasible[136](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=136) . Enrollment that was 63% U.S.-based supported applicability to the U.S. population[137](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=137) .


For dostarlimab, FDA reported a BICR-confirmed ORR of 41.6% across 209 patients[621](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=621) . It also noted 15 tumor types, some represented by only one or two patients[625](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=625) . Before submission, FDA had warned that most of approximately 200 patients had endometrial or colon cancer, with only about 30 having other tumor types[129](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=129) . Confirmatory evidence was therefore to come from at least 300 patients with representation beyond endometrial and gastrointestinal tumors[625](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=625) .


For trastuzumab deruxtecan, FDA stated that DP-02 alone included too few tumor types to support an agnostic indication, because tumors studied separately (NSCLC, gastric and colorectal) were excluded. FDA also noted the mismatch between the 6.4 mg/kg gastric dose and the proposed 5.4 mg/kg agnostic dose[168](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=168) . The multi-study IHC 3+ dataset was acceptable to support filing[166](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=166) . FDA separately analyzed a three-trial pool so that breast cancer patients from DB-01 would not mask safety signals[288](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=288) . It found safety consistent across tumor types because patients, despite differing histologies, were in similar prior-therapy settings[291](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=291) .


#### When FDA declined a tissue-agnostic claim


Zenocutuzumab (Bizengri, BLA 761352) shows the limit of the approach. FDA found the eNRGy tissue-agnostic package inadequate. NSCLC and pancreatic adenocarcinoma made up over 78% of every analysis population, and confirmed responses occurred in only four of eight tumor types[161](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=161)[191](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=191) . FDA cited differing response magnitudes across tumor types[162](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=162) . It also said heterogeneous prior treatment prevented a judgment on whether NSCLC response rates improved on available therapy[163](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=163) , and advised excluding expanded-access patients from the primary pooled analysis because of potential heterogeneity[164](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=164) . FDA allowed tissue-agnostic development to continue in eNRGy for a possible future application[159](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=159) .


### Tumor-specific approvals from a single basket cohort


Several approvals relied on one disease cohort within a basket trial. Here the reviewer commentary concerns single-arm inference more than cross-tumor pooling.


- **Keytruda, cervical cancer (KEYNOTE-158 Cohort E):** Reviewers described an adaptive basket trial with ongoing review of accrual and potentially multiple interim analyses[323](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=323) . No power calculations were built into the overall design[736](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=736) . FDA did not integrate KEYNOTE-028 data because trial designs, doses and populations differed[34](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=34) . The statistical review stated that "no inferential procedures were used to evaluate results from this single arm study," that efficacy rested on response magnitude and duration, and that "time-to-event endpoints are uninterpretable without a comparator arm"[735](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=735) . Patient characteristics were considered generalizable to the U.S. population despite largely international enrollment[32](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=32) .
- **Zepzelca, SCLC (Study B-005):** The single-arm basket trial was the primary efficacy evidence[69](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=69) . FDA found investigator and IRC response results consistent[699](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=699) and accepted response rate as an endpoint because such shrinkage would not occur without therapy[701](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=701) . Earlier, FDA had said the cohort would not support accelerated approval, citing a small platinum-resistant subgroup and a CI lower bound below 12%[706](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=706)[707](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=707) . PFS and OS were "uninterpretable without a comparator arm"[705](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=705) , and continued approval depended on a confirmatory trial[708](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=708) .
- **Trodelvy, mTNBC (IMMU-132-01):** Reviewers accepted an ORR of 33.3% with median DOR of 7.7 months in 108 patients[539](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=539) , with no notable statistical issues[541](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=541) . They cautioned that central review covered only selected responders (n=55)[544](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=544) . FDA had earlier rejected a 31-patient cohort as insufficient on its own[545](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=545) .
- **Zelboraf, Erdheim-Chester disease (VE-BASKET):** The application rested primarily on ORR from a single-arm, open-label, nonrandomized phase II trial with 22 ECD patients[574](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=574)[575](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=575) . The Division agreed that no ECD companion diagnostic was needed because of the disease's rarity, with local BRAF V600 testing permitted[65](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=65)[572](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=572) . PK appeared similar across melanoma, NSCLC and ECD[64](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=64) .


### Master protocols and platform trials outside oncology


#### PALM: Inmazeb and Ebanga


The PALM review gives FDA's clearest explicit statement on the value of master protocols. Under "Trial Design," reviewers listed the advantages: evaluating multiple treatments against a shared active investigational control, adding or removing arms, reducing sample size, and using common infrastructure with consistent data collection[224](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=224) . On multiplicity, reviewers acknowledged there is no statistical consensus, but noted the view that each treatment-versus-control comparison can be considered a separate trial[224](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=224) . Because the three investigational products belonged to different sponsors, and no sponsor had multiple chances to "win," no multiplicity adjustment was considered necessary[402](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=402) .


The main limitation reviewers identified was the comparator. Using investigational ZMapp rather than optimized standard of care alone raised interpretability concerns[403](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=403) . The master protocol allowed either control, and the DRC selected ZMapp plus oSOC[404](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=404) . The trial was open-label, and two randomization block sizes were used to reduce selection bias[401](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=401) . The DSMB stopped assignment to ZMapp and remdesivir after an interim analysis showed superiority of REGN-EB3 and mAb114[406](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=406)[374](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=374) . The Inmazeb reviewer reported a 17.2 percentage-point reduction in 28-day mortality versus ZMapp (33.8% vs 51.0%), following a prespecified stopping criterion[375](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=375) . FDA considered the dose "demonstrated to be effective in comparison to the active control"[410](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=410) . The Ebanga team found no issues in assessing superiority over ZMapp[372](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=372) and judged trial conduct adequate[379](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=379) . FDA also noted that the absence of PK sampling in infected PALM participants prevented exposure-response analysis[223](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=223) .


#### SURMOUNT-OSA: Zepbound


FDA called GPIF a "basket-type master protocol" supporting two independent randomized, placebo-controlled trials, GPI1 (no PAP) and GPI2 (on PAP)[220](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=220)[221](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=221) . Each trial had its own placebo group[422](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=422) . FDA had recommended two adequate and well-controlled trials, and the applicant confirmed there would be no shared placebo and no pooled efficacy analysis[423](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=423) . FDA agreed in January 2024 that efficacy would not be pooled[425](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=425) . The April 2024 SAP nevertheless pooled the PROMIS PRO key secondary endpoints across the intervention-specific appendices[426](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=426) .


Reviewers rejected that pooling for two reasons. Baseline PAP use could confound PRO assessment, and pooling a key endpoint was inconsistent with independent substantiation from more than one investigation[427](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=427) . The separate-trial PRO results were therefore treated as exploratory, outside the multiplicity hierarchy[428](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=428)[429](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=429) . The Division Director still described GPI1 and GPI2 as two adequate and well-controlled trials providing substantial evidence of effectiveness[430](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=430) . For sponsors, the lesson is that a shared master protocol can deliver two independent pivotal trials, but FDA would not accept pooling the key PRO endpoints across them.


#### RECOVERY: tocilizumab


Actemra labeling shared by BLA 125276 (intravenous, the COVID-19 formulation) and BLA 125472 states that COVID-19 efficacy "was based on RECOVERY," a randomized, controlled, open-label platform study, with EMPACTA as support[451](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=451)[454](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=454) . The control was standard of care alone, the primary endpoint was time to death through Day 28, and 82% of patients were on systemic corticosteroids at baseline[457](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=457)[458](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=458)[459](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=459) . RECOVERY data also appear in the Tofidence and Avtozma biosimilar records[455](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=455)[456](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=456) . The FDA review documents cited here do not contain reviewer commentary on RECOVERY's open-label design or usual-care control.


#### Comirnaty


CBER reviewers relied on Substudies A and C of C4591031, "A Phase 3 Master Protocol To Evaluate Additional Dose(S) Of BNT162b2," as supportive safety and immunogenicity data for a third dose[339](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=339)[340](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=340) . Only two of six substudies were presented, with limited follow-up[341](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=341) . The cited passages contain no design-specific appraisal.


### Supportive rather than pivotal use


Master protocols also appear in approval packages in secondary roles:


- **Lumakras (NDA 214665, S-9):** Study 20190135, a phase 1b master protocol, contributed cross-tumor integrated safety data. The pivotal study was the separate randomized Study 20190172[227](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=227)[229](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=229)[319](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=319) .
- **Litfulo (NDA 215830):** B7931005, footnoted as an "umbrella trial design" testing brepocitinib and ritlecitinib, supported lymphocyte-count modeling[101](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=101)[102](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=102)[100](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=100) .
- **Ibtrozi (NDA 219713):** AB-106-C205, an NTRK basket study, was listed only under studies supporting safety[46](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=46) .
- **Norvir and Viracept:** Pediatric HIV master protocols (PACTG 366, a phase I/II master protocol, and the Rolling Arm Master protocols) contributed pediatric PK and screening data[236](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=236)[243](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=243) .


### What FDA said about a proposed platform trial


The Talvey (BLA 761342) record contains FDA's most detailed critique of a platform design, though the trial was proposed and is not shown to have supported approval[384](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=384)[70](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=70) . FDA generally agreed with the master-protocol approach[384](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=384) but raised these concerns:


- Operational complexity could cause miscommunication that compromises patient safety, so FDA recommended a dedicated IND[386](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=386) .
- The control must reflect current U.S. standard of care, with enrollment suspended if that standard changes[387](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=387) .
- Comparisons across enrollment periods could introduce bias even with stratification by time[388](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=388) .
- Adding arms could change control-arm sample-size requirements and eligibility, and FDA asked for plans to handle this[389](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=389) .
- Multiple hypotheses tested against one control raise study-wide multiplicity concerns that could weaken registration evidence[390](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=390)[391](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=391) .


### Recurring reviewer themes


**Strengths FDA credited**


- Efficiency through shared infrastructure, shared controls and the ability to add or drop arms[224](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=224) .
- Feasibility in rare, molecularly defined populations where randomization is impractical or inappropriate[189](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=189)[136](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=136)[474](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=474) .
- Strong biological rationale and consistent, durable responses across histologies as the basis for pooling[149](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=149)[186](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=186)[305](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=305) .
- Response rate as an interpretable endpoint because tumor shrinkage is not expected without treatment[701](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=701)[668](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=668) .
- BICR and prespecified analyses to limit measurement bias in single-arm cohorts[475](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=475)[476](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=476) .


**Limitations FDA flagged**


- No inferential testing, and time-to-event endpoints uninterpretable without a comparator[735](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=735)[705](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=705)[543](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=543) .
- Missing sample-size or power justification[671](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=671)[736](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=736) .
- Sparse or skewed tumor-type representation and unreliable subgroup estimates[625](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=625)[673](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=673)[134](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=134)[161](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=161) .
- Pooling that conflicts with independent substantiation or mixes heterogeneous populations[427](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=427)[164](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=164) .
- Shared-control choices (an investigational comparator, changing standard of care, nonconcurrent controls) that affect interpretability[403](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=403)[387](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=387)[388](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=388) .
- Accelerated approval with postmarketing requirements to broaden tumor coverage or confirm benefit[625](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=625)[135](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=135)[151](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=151)[708](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=708) .


### Open questions for further research


Some reviewer analyses were not found in the documents examined here. These include FDA's review of the BRAF V600E tissue-agnostic approval for dabrafenib plus trametinib (the retrieved Tafinlar records discuss the later pediatric low-grade glioma application)[524](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=524)[526](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=526) , the review underlying pembrolizumab's TMB-H indication (only labeling text was retrieved)[507](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-approvals-based-on-basket-umbrella?showSourceNumber=507) , and FDA reviewer commentary on RECOVERY's design. Each is a natural follow-up for teams benchmarking a master-protocol submission strategy.
